title: Unemployment Benefit Claims — Schedule of Monetary Determination Figures by Program
content:
The figures below are the program figures that a monetary determination on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record reads: the wage test, the weekly benefit amount divisor, floor and ceiling, the rounding of benefit figures, the record that establishes base-period wages, and the redetermination request window. Each program of Unemployment Benefit Claims has its own row.

## Wage test and weekly amount figures

| Program | Minimum high-quarter wages (USD) | Minimum ratio of base-period wages to high-quarter wages | Alternate base period tested | Divisor applied to high-quarter wages | Weekly benefit floor (USD per week) | Weekly benefit ceiling before dependency allowance (USD per week) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Regular State Unemployment Insurance | 1950.00 | 1.5 | Yes | 26 | 75.00 | 572.00 |
| Unemployment Compensation for Federal Employees (UCFE) | 1950.00 | 1.5 | Yes | 26 | 75.00 | 572.00 |
| Unemployment Compensation for Ex-Servicemembers (UCX) | 1950.00 | 1.5 | Yes | 26 | 75.00 | 572.00 |
| Combined Wage Claim (CWC) | 1950.00 | 1.5 | Yes | 26 | 75.00 | 572.00 |
| Extended Benefits (EB) | 1950.00 | 1.5 | No | 26 | 75.00 | 572.00 |
| Trade Readjustment Allowances (TRA) | 1950.00 | 1.5 | No | 26 | 75.00 | 572.00 |
| Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA) | 0.00 (no wage test) | 0 (not applied) | No | 26 | 215.50 | 572.00 |

## Wage record and redetermination window

| Program | Record that establishes base-period wages or employment | Redetermination request window (calendar days after the monetary determination date) |
|---|---|---|
| Regular State Unemployment Insurance | State quarterly wage records | 21 |
| Unemployment Compensation for Federal Employees (UCFE) | ES-931 federal findings | 21 |
| Unemployment Compensation for Ex-Servicemembers (UCX) | DD-214 (Member 4) | 21 |
| Combined Wage Claim (CWC) | IB-4 interstate wage transfer | 21 |
| Extended Benefits (EB) | The parent regular claim | 21 |
| Trade Readjustment Allowances (TRA) | The trade adjustment petition and employer wages | 21 |
| Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA) | Proof of employment or self-employment | 21 |

**Rounding of benefit figures.** For every program the weekly benefit amount, the maximum benefit amount and each weekly payable amount are rounded down to the whole dollar.

## Notes on reading the schedule

- A minimum high-quarter wages figure of 0.00 means the program has no wage test; a ratio of 0 means the ratio test is not applied.
- "Alternate base period tested" states whether the alternate base period (the last four completed calendar quarters) is tested when the standard base period fails.
- The weekly benefit ceiling is the ceiling before any dependency allowance; the floor and the ceiling are the limits applied to the weekly benefit amount after the divisor.
- The Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA) weekly floor is 215.50; every other program's floor is 75.00.

### Hypothetical reading

A hypothetical Regular State Unemployment Insurance claimant whose highest-paid quarter shows 7800.00 meets the 1950.00 high-quarter figure; the ratio test then asks whether total base-period wages reach 1.5 times 7800.00, that is 11700.00. The figures in this example other than the schedule entries are illustrations only.
